provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The factory works out where the parts of the canonical 20x11 layout land after the transform. It builds a label grid in canonical coordinates (legend rows 0-5, divider row 6, canvas rows 7-19) and applies the stated D4 transform to it: reverse each row if d4>=4, then rotate clockwise d4%4 times. From the result it reads three facts: whether the divider is a visible row or a visible column, its index, and whether the legend lies before or after it. It also fills in two colour constants: the background, palette[7], and the divider colour, palette[6]. The emitted program works directly in visible coordinates. It finds the full line of the divider colour in the known orientation, preferring the expected index. This means a marker that happens to share colour 6 does not confuse it. It splits the grid into the legend side and the canvas side and finds single-colour 4-connected components in the legend. Components of size>1 are the 3x3 colour blocks; single pixels are markers. Each marker is paired with the block whose extent along the divider-parallel axis contains it, falling back to the nearest block. The output is a background canvas the same size as the visible canvas region, with every non-background canvas pixel replaced by a 3x3 block of its paired legend colour, centred on it and clipped at the edges. This matches the generator under all D4s: the canvas sub-rectangle transforms consistently with the output, and a centred 3x3 stamp is unaffected by rotation or reflection. The fixtures agree with this single uniform rule.
draft_notes.limitations: Assumes the generator's fixed canonical layout: 20x11 input with legend in rows 0-5, divider at row 6 and canvas below. That layout fixes the expected divider index and which side holds the legend, though the divider is still detected from the grid by colour and fullness. If a marker colour has no matching block, the marker stamps its own colour. The generator never produces overlapping stamps, so stamp order is unspecified for overlaps.
